Legs.Subject: ReciprocalDivisor32.Divide: ceil(2^64/d) high multiply for uint dividends and nonzero uint divisors
Legs.Against: Oracles.ReciprocalDivision: BigInteger /; every divisor 1..65535, powers of two and neighbours through 2^31, uint.MaxValue, and full-width sampled operands; each divisor probes d-1, d, d+1 and the last uint multiple and its lower neighbour

Legs.Subject: Zero construction refuses; the default value divides by one at zero, one, the signed boundary and uint.MaxValue. uint input types enforce the exact operand envelope.
MultisetDigest.Add over sampled multisets with repeats: the digest of each multiset
Legs.Against: Oracles.MultisetDigest: the BigInteger sum of InvertibleBitMix.Mix64 over the elements, reduced modulo 2^64
Legs.Shared: InvertibleBitMix.Mix64, whose own law pins it

Legs.Subject: Empty is zero; every order of one multiset digests equally; Remove undoes Add from any digest; Union of two digests equals adding both multisets' elements to Empty.
PackedIntPairComparer: full-word equality and wrapped Fibonacci product's upper word
Legs.Against: Oracles.PackedPairHash: unbounded BigInteger multiplication with an explicit modulo mask and decimal multiplier; equality checked against long ==, including reflexivity

Legs.Subject: Leb128: Write is the minimal spelling and TryRead reads it back at every group boundary of a 64-bit value; a value over the accepted bits, a truncated spelling, an over-long spelling and (when required) a padded spelling are refused
SequenceEqualityComparer: arrays, read-only lists and spans with equal elements in order are equal and hash alike; a differing element, length or order is unequal; null equals only null
SplitMix64.NextUInt64: the golden-gamma counter through the 64-bit finalizer, the published stream
Legs.Against: The first five words of seed 1234567 as the SplitMix64 reference implementation and its published test vectors give them; State restores the stream

Legs.Subject: PartitionPoint.Of: the first index a monotone test rejects, found by binary search
Legs.Against: A linear count of the accepted prefix, over every prefix length of runs with duplicate keys, lower-bound and upper-bound tests, and the empty run
